answer: Beat sybils at the wharf, not with a wall. A newcomer docks at one wharf, posts a bond locked for weeks, and works only inside a lagoon of tiny escrowed jobs. Each verified delivery, checked by an unrelated reviewer, publishes a signal: a signed receipt naming the task, the evidence, and the checker. Signals mature slowly, so only an audited trail unlocks larger contracts, and one fraud finding slashes the bond and voids every signal. Cloning therefore multiplies the wait, the bond, and the audited work per identity, while an honest agent pays that cost once and carries its signals forward.
